summary: Four small setting conflicts found while building bible/costumes.json. Each has a working value in costumes.json so nothing is blocked; each needs a ruling or a wording fix upstream.

findings.issue: The Caterpillar card gives his gown as 'deep cornflower-to-slate blue'. style.json says cornflower blue is Alice's alone and no other character wears it.
findings.working_value: COS-019 uses slate blue with a moss-green sheen (the Caterpillar palette in style.json user_refs). No cornflower.
findings.requested_action: appearance owner (via memory-bible) changes the card wording to 'slate blue', or art-director confirms an exception.
findings.closed_note: 2026-09-23 superseded by BIB-0027: COS-019/COS-052 are now unclothed CGI animals (DEF-p4-cr-costume-001-a)

findings.issue: CR-012 allows in-world lettering only for DRINK ME, EAT ME, W. RABBIT and ORANGE MARMALADE. The Hatter's hat price ticket ('In this style 10/6') is required by the Bible but is not on that list.
findings.working_value: COS-015 keeps a small paper ticket 'marked 10/6' on the hat.
findings.requested_action: art-director adds the Hatter's '10/6' price ticket to the CR-012 whitelist.
findings.ruling: KEEP the ticket as a named exception to CR-012. 'In this style 10/6' is a canon detail of the Hatter's hat, so under this order's rule (never silently drop a source-text detail) the lettering stays and the closed list grows by one named item. COS-015 is unchanged and now carries the ruling in a lettering_ruling block.
findings.required_style_amendment: bible/style.json CR-012 must add "the Hatter's hat price ticket, marked 10/6" to its allowed in-world lettering list, in period hand-lettering, with the Art Nouveau no-poster-lettering clause untouched.
findings.handed_off_to: 06-art/art-director via qa/defects/DEF-p4-style-003.json (style.json is that agent's file and is frozen at H2; memory-bible did not edit it)

files: bible/costumes.json COS-012, COS-001 variants, COS-007/008/010 variants
findings.issue: Some worn items could belong to either costume or prop: the Knave's wrist chain at the trial (ch011-p01), the White Rabbit's kid glove that Alice puts on (ch002-p14), and the spectacles worn by the King, Queen and White Rabbit.
findings.working_value: The Knave's chain is written into COS-012 visual_en as a worn item. The glove and spectacles are outfit variants only, and so are not in any default visual_en.
findings.requested_action: orchestrator decides who owns these items; if prop takes the chain, costume will drop it from COS-012 visual_en and cross-reference the prop.
findings.ruling: Ownership rule of record: an item that stays on one wearer for its whole screen life is COSTUME, even when it is put on or taken off as business; an item that changes hands, is consumed, or drives a plot beat is a PROP. Therefore -- the Knave's wrist cuffs and chain stay in COS-012 and are deliberately not registered in props.json; the King's, Queen's and White Rabbit's spectacles stay costume outfit variants (COS-010, COS-008, COS-007); the White Rabbit's white kid gloves and fan stay a prop (PROP-white-kid-gloves-and-fan) and the two costume variants that show them now carry a prop_ref. Nothing moved file, so no downstream artefact is stale.

findings.issue: J09 (cockatoo juror) has a 'white coat'. The crowd card keeps white coats off ensembles so the White Rabbit keeps the white read, and he stands near the jury-box as herald.
findings.working_value: COS-052 dresses J09 in a pale cream coat; the white crest hair is left to the appearance card.
findings.requested_action: appearance owner confirms the change or asks for white to be restored.
findings.closed_note: 2026-09-23 superseded by BIB-0027: COS-019/COS-052 are now unclothed CGI animals (DEF-p4-cr-costume-001-a)

impact: None of these blocks p4-char-concept or p4-costume-sheet. Rulings only affect wording.

resolution.authority: H2 art-style lock, gate G4, approval ba96732d (runs/g4/gate.json)
resolution.summary: a and d were already superseded by BIB-0027; b is ruled in costume's favour with the style.json amendment handed to 06-art/art-director (DEF-p4-style-003); c is ruled with an explicit costume-vs-prop ownership rule. Nothing left open on this ticket for costume or memory-bible.
